observations.text: Section 2's pruning row reads 'for items no longer in the inventory'; the repaired code prunes 'items whose declaration left the machine (stamp path gone), or unstamped trees the inventory does not claim'. The two agree wherever section 8's trigger ('an item is removed from the ring') is the event; they differ only in the single-vantage reading B1.24 showed destroys other projects' environments. Section 0 closes the decisions, so this is reported: a successor doc change should reword the section-2 row to section 8's trigger (one line, in research/workflow-ladder-spec-2026-09-02.md, outside U12's license).

B1.26's deviation from C1's smallest_change (resolve inside install(), not ensure()) is the better cut: install is exported and callable alone, and the outcome's human-facing `command` text stays 'npm ci' rather than a machine path. The consequence B1.26 predicted holds: the pre-existing reuse check keeps its ('npm','ci') expectation and a new check crosses the spawn instead. Accepted.

A stamped environment whose declaration is still on disk but whose item left every inventory (e.g. a bundle un-imported while its clone survives) is kept, not pruned. Not destructive, not the section-8 event, and scripts/orchflows_home.py:327 removes a bundle's clone on remove, so the declaration normally leaves with the item. Noted only.

The real-host reading R1b ran `npm ci` for real in a temp item (no dependencies; 'up to date, audited 1 package in 14s'); the temp tree was removed by the script. Nothing in any ring, home or project was touched by the readings.
